title: Clopen tensor identities and formal composition from the Cartesian square
statement: For either Mode and every normalized ringed Cartesian open square Input d, SiteSquare t, Operations o, Assertion a and open immersion s:A→d.U', let v be any Data o s of [def-sf-clopen-comparison-tensor-data]. Then Equations a v holds: (1) the Cartesian tensor identity P_p(delta_i);beta;b_!(mu_q);b_!(1 tensor theta inverse)=mu_p;(beta tensor 1);delta_b; (2) rho followed by extension of the restriction tensor map equals rho tensor identity followed by delta_s; (3) delta_b followed by b_!delta_s equals deltaK; (4) the full alpha tensor identity is their composite, with the displayed theta factors. Every equality holds on the whole unbounded derived category, naturally in its derived objects, with no flatness or boundedness hypotheses.

proof.text:
localize the ordinary unit-counit normalization. Under the resulting reverse
adjunction, both sides of the clopen tensor square transpose to the restriction
tensor comparison, using its naturality and the triangle identity. Transpose the
inverses of the composite-open comparisons under the composite adjunction; tensor
naturality and the formula for its unit identify them. Finally expand alpha and
paste the Cartesian, clopen and composite-open identities, moving rho through the
tensor comparison by naturality.
